question: A patient uses crushed fresh leaves on a swollen joint. What kind of poultice is this?

options.A: An herbal poultice
options.B: A surgical poultice
options.C: A chemical poultice
options.D: A synthetic poultice

explanation: Using fresh plants or leaves directly falls under the category of traditional herbal poultices. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary neurotransmitter blocked by anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Serotonin
options.B: Dopamine
options.C: Norepinephrine
options.D: Acetylcholine

explanation: Anticholinergic drugs specifically target and block acetylcholine receptors in the nervous system. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h1)

question: Who is the focus of medical isolation compared to quarantine?

options.A: Travelers arriving from a foreign country
options.B: People who are currently sick with an infection
options.C: Healthcare workers who finished their shift
options.D: Healthy family members of a sick patient

explanation: Isolation separates individuals who already have a confirmed or suspected active infection from others. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which emergency bedside maneuver helps control bleeding temporarily by sandwiching the uterus between two hands?

options.A: External cephalic version
options.B: Controlled cord traction
options.C: Fundal displacement
options.D: Bimanual compression

explanation: Bimanual compression is a lifesaving skill! You place one hand inside the vagina and the other on the abdominal wall to squeeze the bleeding uterine walls together.

question: Why is it so important for nurses to check for drug interactions between ART and other medications?

options.A: Other medications will instantly turn HIV into a completely different virus
options.B: Patients are forbidden from taking pain relief while on ARVs
options.C: Liver enzyme interactions can dangerously lower or raise drug levels in the blood
options.D: Taking two pills at once causes them to physically dissolve in the throat

explanation: Spot on! ARVs interact with liver enzymes. If we aren't careful, another drug can accidentally wash the ARVs out too fast or build them up to toxic levels.

question: How do nurses directly help make a hospital Drug Revolving Fund successful?

options.A: By auditing the central bank accounts of the hospital management
options.B: By setting the retail profit markups for all essential medicines
options.C: By importing foreign pharmaceuticals directly from overseas factories
options.D: By providing feedback on drug stock levels and ward consumption

explanation: As nurses, we work directly with patients and medications every day. Spotting low stock early and letting pharmacy know helps keep the supply chain smooth.

question: Where in the digestive tract does the absorption of almost all nutrients happen?

options.A: Esophagus
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Large intestine
options.D: Small intestine

explanation: The small intestine is the superstar of absorption! Its lining is specially designed to soak up digested nutrients straight into the bloodstream.

question: How do pressures in the lungs and body change right after birth?

options.A: Both lung and body resistance drop together
options.B: Lung resistance drops while body resistance rises
options.C: Both lung and body resistance increase together
options.D: Lung resistance rises while body resistance drops

explanation: Expanding the lungs lowers pulmonary resistance, while cutting the placenta raises systemic resistance. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h4)

question: What is a virtual health community?

options.A: An online space where people connect for health support
options.B: A physical clinic equipped with virtual reality headsets
options.C: A government database of all registered nurses in a country
options.D: An emergency ambulance fitted with satellite navigation

explanation: You got it! Think of online support groups, health forums, and social media pages where people share health tips.

question: What is the main benefit of using the 'teach-back' method during patient education?

options.A: It reduces the cost of buying medical equipment for the clinic
options.B: It measures the exact blood pressure of the client instantly
options.C: It eliminates the need for any further nursing documentation
options.D: It confirms whether the person truly understands the instructions

explanation: Brilliant! Asking patients to explain things back in their own words helps you catch and clear up any confusion before they leave.

question: Why should nurses take time to understand a patient's cultural or identity group?

options.A: Identity groups are the only source of funding for hospitals
options.B: It prevents patients from ever catching infectious diseases
options.C: Patients often follow health advice that respects their cultural norms
options.D: It allows the nurse to change the patient's religious beliefs

explanation: Spot on! When we respect a patient's cultural background, trust grows, and they are much more likely to follow our health guidance.

question: What is a common barrier that nurses frequently encounter in community mental health care?

options.A: Too many available hospital beds in rural areas
options.B: Chronic funding shortages and cultural stigma
options.C: An overwhelming surplus of trained psychiatrists
options.D: Excessive community demand for group therapy

explanation: Lack of financial resources and social stigma against mental illness are major obstacles to providing effective community care. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h8)

question: What is the most common correctable physical cause of male infertility?

options.A: Varicocele
options.B: Testicular torsion
options.C: Klinefelter syndrome
options.D: Cryptorchidism

explanation: A varicocele is an enlarged set of veins in the scrotum that doctors can surgically repair to help restore normal fertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: What is the main job of target cell receptors in the endocrine system?

options.A: To recognize and securely bind to specific circulating hormones
options.B: To destroy excess hormones before they reach the bloodstream
options.C: To filter metabolic waste products out of cellular tissue
options.D: To manufacture new cholesterol for hormone production

explanation: Think of receptors as custom locks, and hormones as the matching keys. They ensure that only the right message triggers the right cell!

question: In the HEADS adolescent screening tool, what does the letter 'S' stand for?

options.A: Skeletal strength
options.B: Sexuality
options.C: Sleep hygiene
options.D: Skin integrity

explanation: Spot on! In HEADS, 'S' stands for Sexuality (and Suicide), guiding the nurse to check in on relationships and reproductive health.

question: Why is folic acid routinely given to women who are planning to get pregnant?

options.A: To stimulate rapid bone growth and skeletal mineralization in the fetus.
options.B: To prevent neural tube defects in early fetal development.
options.C: To increase the total daily caloric intake during the first trimester.
options.D: To protect the mother from developing severe iron-deficiency anemia.

explanation: Folic acid is a superstar for early pregnancy! It helps the baby's neural tube close properly, long before many mums even know they are expecting.

question: What is a crucial safety rule when applying a new transdermal patch?

options.A: Remove the old patch before placing the new one
options.B: Place the new patch directly on top of the old patch
options.C: Cut the new patch in half to adjust the daily dose
options.D: Apply the patch to a hairy area for better adhesion

explanation: Leaving an old patch on while putting on a new one can cause an accidental overdose because of extra medicine absorption. Safety check passed!

question: Which hormone is the main driver of male reproductive development?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Great job! Testosterone is the key male sex hormone made in the testes that shapes male physical traits and reproductive function.

question: What is a main reason fresh fruits spoil so fast after harvest in hot climates?

options.A: Excessive consumption of vegetables by local farmers
options.B: Inadequate cold storage and refrigeration facilities
options.C: Overly strict international export quality standards
options.D: The use of organic seeds instead of commercial hybrids

explanation: Correct! Without good refrigeration in hot weather, fresh produce unfortunately goes bad before it ever gets to market.

question: A patient recovering from surgery suddenly complains of severe shortness of breath and sharp chest pain. What emergency should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: An infected leg ulcer
options.B: A pulmonary embolism from a dislodged blood clot
options.C: A blocked artery in the lower leg
options.D: Advanced Raynaud's syndrome in the fingers

explanation: Watch out for post-op patients! If a clot in the leg breaks loose, it can travel up to the lungs and block blood flow, causing sudden breathlessness and chest pain.

question: Which type of underwear helps prevent moisture buildup and lowers the risk of vulvitis?

options.A: Tight synthetic nylon shapewear
options.B: Polyester tights worn all day
options.C: Rubberized protective shorts
options.D: 100% cotton underwear

explanation: Cotton breathes easily and prevents trapped moisture, which is key because yeast and bacteria love warm, damp places. Simple prevention advice makes great nursing practice!

question: Which of these is considered a metabolic risk factor for non-communicable diseases?

options.A: Living in an urban area
options.B: Daily cigarette smoking
options.C: Low dietary fiber intake
options.D: Raised blood pressure

explanation: Great job! Metabolic risk factors happen inside the body's chemistry and biology, such as high blood pressure, high blood sugar, or extra body weight.

question: What actually are cervical polyps?

options.A: Congenital malformations
options.B: Infectious cysts of the vagina
options.C: Benign growths on the cervix
options.D: Malignant tumors of the uterus

explanation: Don't worry, these are non-cancerous growths! They just form on the cervical tissue, meaning they are benign. You've got this!

question: What is the main purpose of a post-incident debriefing or 'hot wash' session?

options.A: To review performance, identify communication failures, and improve future responses
options.B: To audit employee payroll and overtime hours for budget approval
options.C: To assign personal blame and punishment to staff members who made mistakes
options.D: To celebrate the end of the shift with recreational activities

explanation: Debriefs aren't about pointing fingers; they're safe spaces to figure out what went well and what can be fixed for next time.

question: What is a recommended safety item for a patient diagnosed with a chronic seizure disorder to wear at all times?

options.A: A medical alert bracelet
options.B: A portable oxygen tank
options.C: A hard plastic safety helmet
options.D: A bright yellow reflective vest

explanation: A medical alert bracelet provides instant information to bystanders and healthcare workers if the patient has a seizure in public. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h8)

question: Which nursing action is MOST important when caring for a patient with active surgical drains after pancreatic surgery?

options.A: Flush the drainage tubing with sterile water every two hours.
options.B: Monitor and record the amount and color of drainage regularly.
options.C: Clamp all surgical drains shut to prevent accidental fluid loss.
options.D: Change the surrounding skin dressings once every week.

explanation: Keep up the great clinical thinking! Tracking your drain output closely helps you catch dangerous warning signs like bleeding or fistulas early.

question: As a nurse, what is your very first priority when a patient arrives with post-abortion complications?

options.A: Conducting a detailed interview about contraception history
options.B: Reporting the incident immediately to law enforcement
options.C: Asking about her religious and cultural beliefs
options.D: Evaluating airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: Safety first! Emergency nursing always starts with the ABCs to stabilize vital signs and catch shock or heavy bleeding early.

question: Which animal serves as the intermediate host for the beef tapeworm, Taenia saginata?

options.A: Cattle
options.B: Goats
options.C: Pigs
options.D: Dogs

explanation: Well done! Cattle act as the intermediate host for Taenia saginata, carrying the larval cysts in their muscles.

question: What is the main purpose of adaptive equipment in rehabilitation?

options.A: To help clients perform daily tasks independently despite physical limits
options.B: To monitor the daily vital signs of clients living at home
options.C: To speed up the biological knitting of broken bone fragments
options.D: To completely replace the need for physical therapy and exercise

explanation: Spot on! Adaptive tools give patients clever ways to wash, dress, and eat on their own without always needing help.

question: What must form first before a bone can grow using endochondral ossification?

options.A: Primary vascular plexus
options.B: Hyaline cartilage model
options.C: Dense collagenous tendon
options.D: Fibrous connective tissue sheet

explanation: Think of cartilage as a tiny practice sculpture! Endochondral bones need a hyaline cartilage model first, which is later replaced by true bone.

question: Which of these is NOT considered when deciding whether to stop a rescue attempt?

options.A: Duration of the cardiac arrest event
options.B: Initial heart rhythm and response to interventions
options.C: The patient's personal financial status
options.D: Presence of valid do-not-resuscitate documentation

explanation: Clinical care is based entirely on health factors and ethics, never on a patient's wealth or financial status. Good medical ethics at work!

question: A newly formed community health committee has stopped arguing and is now setting clear operational rules. Which stage of development are they in?

options.A: Storming
options.B: Norming
options.C: Forming
options.D: Adjourning

explanation: During the norming stage, the team establishes rules, resolves past conflicts, and builds a cooperative working relationship. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h2)

question: What emergency procedure is used to drain extra fluid from around the heart during cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Thoracentesis
options.B: Cardioversion
options.C: Pericardiocentesis
options.D: Paracentesis

explanation: Pericardiocentesis involves gently passing a needle into the pericardial sac to draw out fluid and relieve dangerous pressure on the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h7)

question: When do vulval varicose veins most commonly show up?

options.A: During puberty
options.B: Immediately after menstruation
options.C: After menopause
options.D: During pregnancy

explanation: Pregnancy is the peak time for this! The body increases its blood volume and puts extra pressure in the pelvis, which makes these veins pop up. Great job thinking through prenatal changes.

question: Which type of topical preparation is best for dry, thick, or scaly skin because it locks in moisture?

options.A: Lotion
options.B: Gel
options.C: Aqueous solution
options.D: Ointment

explanation: Ointments are oil-heavy, creating a protective blanket that stops moisture from escaping. Perfect for dry, scaly skin patches!

question: Which test is most commonly used to check for structural causes of secondary dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Brain CT scan
options.B: Pelvic ultrasound
options.C: Chest X-ray
options.D: Bone density scan

explanation: Correct! An ultrasound is safe, non-invasive, and great for taking a look at the uterus and ovaries.

question: Why is cultural humility important when providing dietary advice?

options.A: All cultures eat the exact same foods anyway
options.B: Food carries deep emotional and cultural meaning for patients
options.C: Patients will report the nurse to the police if local dishes are ignored
options.D: It proves to the doctor that the nurse is well-traveled

explanation: Respecting cultural food practices ensures the patient feels valued and is more likely to engage in constructive health talks. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h6)

question: A nurse notices that an elderly patient living alone has dim lighting and loose rugs. What action best mitigates this risk?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop walking around the house entirely
options.B: Immediately transferring the patient to a nursing home facility
options.C: Conducting a safety assessment and arranging to clear hazards with the family
options.D: Waiting until the next scheduled annual medical checkup

explanation: Identifying hazards early and working with support networks to fix them prevents accidental falls at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h8)

question: Where should you place the two sticky pads on an adult patient's chest?

options.A: Directly in the center of the back and over the stomach
options.B: Upper left chest and lower right side of the abdomen
options.C: Both shoulders near the outer edges of the collarbone
options.D: Upper right chest and lower left side of the ribs

explanation: Placing one pad on the upper right and the other on the lower left creates a diagonal path so the shock travels right across the heart muscle.

question: What is a drug idiosyncrasy?

options.A: A predictable side effect linked to high dosage
options.B: A delayed therapeutic failure of a medication
options.C: An immune-mediated hypersensitivity reaction
options.D: An abnormal and unpredictable drug reaction

explanation: Think of an idiosyncrasy as a weird, unexpected reaction to a drug that nobody could have seen coming. You've got this!

question: What is the primary objective of gathering psychosocial data in a hospital setting?

options.A: To force the client to change their personal lifestyle habits immediately
options.B: To shape safe, individual nursing care that addresses emotional and social needs
options.C: To prove that the client has no underlying mental health challenges
options.D: To reduce the amount of time nurses spend talking to family members

explanation: The information gathered helps nurses create care plans that treat the whole person, not just the physical disease. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main idea behind the Essential Medicines Concept?

options.A: The mandatory use of expensive imported brand-name drugs over generics
options.B: A select list of priority drugs that meet the healthcare needs of the majority
options.C: Stocking every single pharmaceutical formulation ever invented in every clinic
options.D: Allowing patients to dispense their own prescription drugs without guidance

explanation: Essential medicines are a carefully picked list of priority drugs that treat the most common health needs of everyday people effectively and cheaply.

question: Why can nystatin oral liquid be used safely for mouth thrush without causing major body-wide side effects?

options.A: It is completely neutralized by normal saliva enzymes
options.B: It is poorly absorbed from the digestive tract into the blood
options.C: It breaks down instantly upon touching the oral mucosa
options.D: It only targets bacterial cell walls instead of human cells

explanation: Spot on! Nystatin stays right where it is needed in the mouth or gut. Because very little enters the bloodstream, whole-body side effects are rare.

question: A nurse needs to draw medication from a multidose vial for another patient. Which of these actions is unsafe?

options.A: Swabbing the rubber top of the vial with an alcohol wipe before piercing
options.B: Using a brand new, sterile syringe and needle for drawing up the dose
options.C: Checking the expiration date printed on the label of the vial
options.D: Leaving a previously used dispensing needle inserted in the vial rubber septum

explanation: Never leave a needle stuck inside a multidose vial! It acts like an open door for bacteria to crawl inside and contaminate the medicine for the next patient.

question: Why are compression bands sometimes placed on the patient's abdomen during an IVP?

options.A: To push the contrast dye through the bloodstream much faster
options.B: To prevent the patient from moving around on the hard x-ray table
options.C: To keep the intravenous needle securely taped inside the vein
options.D: To slow urine flow and keep the upper renal system filled with dye

explanation: Abdominal compression temporarily traps the contrast in the kidneys and ureters, making those structures easier to see on the x-ray films. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h5)

question: When public health workers talk about 'social capital', what do they mean?

options.A: The physical buildings like schools, markets, and town halls
options.B: Local networks, groups, and cooperatives that foster mutual support
options.C: The total financial cash stored in commercial banks in the area
options.D: The amount of government grants allocated for road construction

explanation: Social capital is all about 'we are in this together.' It's the trust, friendships, and local groups neighbors rely on to help each other out in times of need.

question: Why is it so important to counsel clients about possible changes in their monthly bleeding before putting in an implant?

options.A: Menstrual cycles will completely stop forever within the first week of insertion in all women
options.B: Clients must know that heavy bleeding will require them to take iron pills every single day
options.C: Changes in bleeding indicate that the implant has slipped out of position into the muscle
options.D: Unpredictable bleeding patterns are common and represent the main reason clients request early removal

explanation: No surprises! Giving a heads-up about spotting or lighter periods helps clients stay calm and prevents unnecessary panic or removing the implant too soon.

question: What does a modified radical mastectomy involve?

options.A: Removal of only the small tumor lump while preserving the rest of the breast
options.B: Surgical removal of the entire breast along with the axillary lymph nodes
options.C: Radiation therapy directed strictly at the skin without touching deep tissue
options.D: Daily administration of oral chemotherapy pills without any surgery

explanation: It means taking out the whole breast tissue plus the armpit lymph nodes to make sure the cancer doesn't linger locally.

question: Why is it important to ask a patient about their job and workplace environment during a social history?

options.A: It helps calculate the exact monthly income of the patient
options.B: It determines how many days off work the patient needs
options.C: Certain jobs expose workers to toxins that cause chronic illness
options.D: It shows whether the patient enjoys their daily job duties

explanation: Well reasoned! Workplace exposures like dust, fumes, or heavy lifting often play a big role in lung or body pains.

question: A newly registered pregnant woman is diagnosed with HIV at her first clinic visit. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to terminate the pregnancy to protect her health.
options.B: Start her on lifelong antiretroviral therapy immediately.
options.C: Wait until her second trimester before prescribing any medications.
options.D: Delay treatment until her CD4 cell count drops below 200.

explanation: Current guidelines recommend prompt initiation of ART for all pregnant women living with HIV, regardless of clinical stage or CD4 count. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h4)

question: Why shouldn't you force a survivor to tell every single detail of their assault right away?

options.A: Forced retelling can trigger severe anxiety and re-traumatize the patient
options.B: Police investigations are always hindered by early patient statements
options.C: Medical records do not need any details about the assault
options.D: Physical examination results become invalid if the patient speaks

explanation: Let survivors take their time. Pressing them to talk too soon can overwhelm them and bring back the trauma.

question: Which of the following is NOT a main cause of peptic ulcers?

options.A: Prolonged use of NSAID medications
options.B: High dietary salt intake alone
options.C: Excessive gastric acid production
options.D: Helicobacter pylori infection

explanation: While spicy or salty foods can irritate an existing ulcer, they don't cause them on their own. Ulcers are mainly caused by H. pylori bacteria and regular use of NSAID painkillers.

question: Which lab results are most important for a nurse to check before starting a patient on anti-bleeding therapy?

options.A: Clotting profiles like PT, INR, and aPTT
options.B: Thyroid hormone panels
options.C: Fasting blood sugar levels
options.D: Routine liver enzymes only

explanation: Always check your patient's clotting baseline! Tests like PT, INR, and aPTT tell you how their blood is currently handling coagulation.

question: Which parts of the body are involved in a lower respiratory tract infection?

options.A: Sinuses, tonsils, and Eustachian tubes
options.B: Nose, pharynx, and larynx
options.C: Oral cavity and epiglottis
options.D: Trachea, bronchi, and alveoli

explanation: Think of the larynx as the dividing line! Anything below it—like the windpipe (trachea), breathing tubes (bronchi), and air sacs (alveoli)—makes up the lower respiratory tract.

question: What is a core day-to-day nursing duty when it comes to reproductive health care?

options.A: Passing national laws regarding reproductive rights
options.B: Performing major obstetric surgical operations independently
options.C: Providing family planning counseling and education
options.D: Manufacturing pharmaceutical contraceptives for hospitals

explanation: Exactly right! Nurses spend a lot of time guiding clients through family planning choices and teaching healthy habits.

question: Why is it so important to treat strep throat (streptococcal pharyngitis) quickly with antibiotics?

options.A: Chronic sinusitis
options.B: Meniere's disease
options.C: Perforated eardrum
options.D: Rheumatic fever

explanation: Spot on! Catching strep throat early and treating it with antibiotics prevents nasty complications like rheumatic fever, which can harm the heart.

question: Why do broad-spectrum antibiotics often trigger a yeast infection in female patients?

options.A: Antibiotics directly stimulate the rapid reproduction of fungal cell walls
options.B: Antibiotics bind directly to antifungal receptors in the mucosal lining
options.C: Antibiotics raise the overall pH of the urine to an overly alkaline level
options.D: Antibiotics kill protective bacteria that normally keep yeast growth under control

explanation: Good bacteria keep the peace in the body. When antibiotics wipe them out, yeast takes over because there's no competition. Simple and clear!

question: What is a vital nursing duty when caring for a pregnant mother with Type III infibulation?

options.A: Advising the patient that no special birth plan is required
options.B: Scheduling an elective hysterectomy at thirty-six weeks
options.C: Instructing the patient to perform self-suturing after delivery
options.D: Anticipating the need for defibulation to allow safe childbirth

explanation: Women with Type III infibulation often need a surgical procedure to open the scar tissue (defibulation) before or during labor so the baby can be born safely.

question: Which contraceptive category offers protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Barrier methods
options.C: Copper intrauterine devices
options.D: Progestin mini-pills

explanation: Barrier methods like condoms physically block bodily fluids, thereby preventing the transmission of infectious organisms as well as sperm. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h5)

question: Which communication skill is most helpful when a patient is trying to process bad medical news?

options.A: Interrupting quickly to save time
options.B: Changing the subject to something cheerful
options.C: Active listening and tolerating silence
options.D: Giving immediate medical advice without asking

explanation: So true! Big news takes time to sink in. Giving patients quiet space and really listening lets them process their emotions without feeling rushed.

question: Where are the free nerve endings that pick up pain mostly found?

options.A: Blood vessels
options.B: Sweat glands
options.C: Epidermis
options.D: Hypodermis

explanation: Well done! These free nerve endings stretch right up into the epidermis so they can easily catch superficial pain and temperature shifts.

question: What is the main idea behind situational leadership?

options.A: Every nurse manager should use an autocratic style
options.B: Only transformational leaders succeed in healthcare
options.C: Leadership style never changes regardless of the task
options.D: Leaders must adapt their style to the context and staff

explanation: Situational leadership requires changing how you lead based on the needs of the staff and the situation at hand. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is a suspected hole (perforation) in the gut a major warning sign against using regular barium?

options.A: The X-ray machine cannot see through leaked barium
options.B: Barium leaks into the abdomen and causes severe inflammation
options.C: The barium will instantly dissolve in the bloodstream
options.D: It will cause immediate kidney failure

explanation: Think of it this way: if the gut has a hole, barium can leak out into the belly and cause a very dangerous reaction and infection. Safety first! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h3)

question: A patient is anxious and has a rapid heart rate before surgery. Which nursing action is best to help calm them?

options.A: Advise the patient to ignore the upcoming surgery entirely
options.B: Leave the patient alone in a brightly lit room to rest
options.C: Guide the patient through slow deep breathing exercises
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink several cups of strong coffee

explanation: Taking slow, deep breaths is a simple, powerful way to quiet the fight-or-flight response, slow down a racing heart, and ease pre-surgery nerves.

question: What should you do if an old gauze dressing is stuck tightly to a healing wound?

options.A: Leave the old gauze stuck and put new dressings on top.
options.B: Moisten it gently with sterile normal saline to loosen it.
options.C: Soak the whole patient in hot soapy water.
options.D: Rip it off quickly with a fast jerk to save time.

explanation: Never rip dry gauze off! A little sterile saline softens the dried fluid and protects that precious new skin underneath.

question: Which group of medications is well-known for damaging hearing (ototoxicity)?

options.A: H2 receptor antagonists
options.B: Aminoglycoside antibiotics
options.C: Short-acting nitrates
options.D: Inhaled corticosteroids

explanation: Watch out for aminoglycoside antibiotics! They can sometimes harm the inner ear and lead to hearing problems if not monitored closely.

question: Why should a nurse keep a patient's cultural background in mind when assessing grief?

options.A: Cultural background is the only factor that influences grieving speed
options.B: Cultural beliefs determine the exact physical symptoms of grief in the body
options.C: Culture prevents people from ever experiencing complicated grief
options.D: Culture dictates how people appropriately express and ritualize mourning

explanation: Spot on! Different cultures have unique ways of mourning and showing sadness. Respecting this helps you give truly patient-centered care.

question: What is the primary health benefit of a PTA providing a borehole in a school?

options.A: It lowers the electricity bills of the school
options.B: It provides mineral water for teachers to sell
options.C: It reduces the spread of waterborne diseases
options.D: It ensures students wash their uniforms daily

explanation: Clean and safe drinking water prevents dangerous waterborne infections such as typhoid and cholera among pupils. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the main job of healthy skin when it comes to protection?

options.A: Regulating the body's hormones
options.B: Making complex carbohydrates
options.C: Producing red blood cells
options.D: Acting as a barrier against germs

explanation: You got this! Healthy skin acts like a natural shield, stopping harmful germs from entering the body.

question: Who founded the Henry Street Settlement and coined the term public health nurse?

options.A: Clara Barton
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Mary Seacole
options.D: Lillian Wald

explanation: Lillian Wald established the Henry Street Settlement in New York City, which became a foundational model for modern public health nursing. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h2)

question: How do airborne pathogens primarily travel to a new host?

options.A: Via large wet respiratory splashes falling straight to the floor
options.B: Through direct physical handshakes with infected individuals
options.C: By clinging to the legs of biting insects or household pets
options.D: As tiny dried droplet nuclei suspended in air currents

explanation: Airborne pathogens are so small and light that they float in the air for hours and travel long distances before being inhaled. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the usual incubation period range for Ebola?

options.B: 1 to 3 hours

options.D: 30 to 60 days

explanation: Correct! Symptoms can show up anywhere from 2 days to 3 weeks after contact. That's why monitoring takes up to 21 days.

question: What is the primary job of the large intestine in the human body?

options.A: Digesting complex fats and proteins
options.B: Filtering waste products out of the blood stream
options.C: Producing most of the body's digestive enzymes
options.D: Absorbing water and forming stool

explanation: The main function of the colon is to take liquid chyme from the small intestine, absorb the water and electrolytes, and turn it into solid feces. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h1)

question: How does political corruption directly hurt maternal and child health programs?

options.A: By building more primary healthcare centers
options.B: By diverting essential medical supplies and funds meant for public clinics
options.C: By lowering the cost of prescription drugs for pregnant women
options.D: By increasing the number of trained midwives in rural villages

explanation: Corruption steals resources meant for the sick, leaving public clinics without basic drugs, working equipment, or safe spaces for mothers. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why should a nurse remind the team to periodically release a retractor during a long operation?

options.A: To allow the metal joints to cool down from body heat
options.B: To clean off accumulated blood and keep the instrument shiny
options.C: To prevent tissue damage and lack of blood supply from constant pressure
options.D: To change the size of the wound opening as the surgery progresses

explanation: Continuous heavy retraction can cut off blood flow to the edges of the wound, leading to localized tissue death. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h6)

question: A 14-year-old boy shows no physical signs of testicular enlargement or puberty yet. How would a nurse document this finding?

options.A: Precocious puberty
options.B: Normal variant
options.C: Delayed puberty
options.D: Acquired gigantism

explanation: You got it! When physical maturation hasn't started by age 14 in males, it is clinically categorized as delayed puberty.

question: What is the recommended period of sexual abstinence before providing a semen sample for analysis?

options.A: Exactly one month
options.B: Twelve to twenty-four hours
options.C: Two to seven days
options.D: One to two full weeks

explanation: A standard abstinence window of two to seven days ensures reliable sperm count and quality measurements. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h6)

question: A ward manager in a public hospital faces severe supply shortages and staff burnout. What is the best way to handle this leadership challenge?

options.A: Waiting passively for central government authorities to fix all facility problems
options.B: Strictly punishing staff members whenever minor supply miscounts occur
options.C: Using adaptive authority to build consensus, mentor staff, and solve problems creatively
options.D: Ignoring hospital protocols entirely and letting junior nurses run the ward

explanation: When resources are tight, great leaders don't just punish—they lean on teamwork, mentor each other, and find creative local solutions to keep caring for patients.

question: How does erratic drug dosing directly affect a patient's body?

options.A: It stabilizes blood pressure within normal ranges
options.B: It helps the liver filter out toxins much faster
options.C: It ensures steady healing and faster tissue repair
options.D: It causes dangerous blood levels leading to toxicity

explanation: Unpredictable timing and dosing create wild spikes in drug concentration, pushing safe levels into toxic territory. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h5)

question: How do conditions like a stroke often lead to urinary incontinence?

options.A: They cause the kidneys to produce excessive amounts of urine
options.B: They permanently shrink the overall size of the bladder
options.C: They destroy the lining of the urinary tract
options.D: They disrupt nerve signals between the brain and the bladder

explanation: Our brain and spinal cord need to talk to the bladder to control peeing. When a stroke damages those pathways, that communication gets mixed up.

question: Why is epidemiologic data vital for community health nurses?

options.A: It eliminates the need for physical examinations in clinics
options.B: It replaces the need to interview sick community members
options.C: It guarantees that funding will increase every fiscal year
options.D: It helps plan effective prevention and allocate resources wisely

explanation: Having accurate data allows nurses to target interventions where they are needed most to protect the community. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which powerful diuretic is most commonly used to quickly clear fluid from a patient's lungs in acute heart failure?

options.A: Spironolactone
options.B: Mannitol
options.C: Furosemide
options.D: Hydrochlorothiazide

explanation: Furosemide is a true workhorse in the ward! It's a loop diuretic that quickly removes extra fluid through urine, giving relief to patients struggling to breathe.

question: What is the very first step a nurse must take before starting CPR on a fallen person?

options.A: Attach the automated external defibrillator
options.B: Ensure the surrounding scene is safe
options.C: Open the airway with a head-tilt maneuver
options.D: Check the patient for a pulse

explanation: Rescuers must check for hazards like fire, live wires, or traffic so they do not become victims themselves. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why are children whose parents are still alive sometimes counted when discussing HIV orphans and vulnerable children?

options.A: They always test positive for the virus at birth
options.B: They live in households where chronic illness severely drains resources
options.C: They possess legal custody over their sick parents
options.D: They are automatically placed in government orphanages

explanation: Even before parents pass away, chronic illness strips a household of income and makes daily survival a struggle. Great insight to keep in mind for community nursing!

question: What clinic setup helps reduce anxiety and shyness for young people seeking care?

options.A: Sharing waiting rooms with adult surgical patients
options.B: Mandatory parental accompaniment for everyone
options.C: Dedicated operating hours specifically for youth
options.D: Strict appointment booking months in advance

explanation: You got it! Special youth hours let adolescents feel less conspicuous and more relaxed among their peers.

question: During which periods can vertical transmission of HIV from mother to child happen?

options.A: Exclusively through routine childhood vaccinations
options.B: During pregnancy, labor, delivery, or breastfeeding
options.C: Only through casual skin-to-skin touch after birth
options.D: Only during the first trimester of pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! The baby can be exposed during pregnancy, birth, or through breast milk afterwards.

question: What is the most important infection control rule when examining multiple patients' ears?

options.A: Washing the entire otoscope handle in boiling water daily
options.B: Wiping only the lens of the otoscope between patients
options.C: Changing the disposable speculum for every single patient
options.D: Using alcohol swabs to clean the inside of the ear canal

explanation: Always use a fresh speculum for each patient to keep germs from spreading from one ear to another. Safety first!

question: What happens to round spermatids during the process called spermiogenesis?

options.A: Primary spermatocytes exchange genetic material through crossing over
options.B: Immature sperm acquire functional motility inside the female tract
options.C: Diploid stem cells multiply through repeated mitotic divisions
options.D: Round spermatids are remodeled into streamlined spermatozoa

explanation: Spermiogenesis is the makeover stage! The round, plain cells grow a tail, pack their head, and turn into sleek swimming sperm.

question: Which touch receptors deep in the skin are best at detecting heavy pressure and fast vibrations?

options.A: Ruffini endings
options.B: Merkel disks
options.C: Pacinian corpuscles
options.D: Meissner corpuscles

explanation: You can do this! Pacinian corpuscles sit deep down and are fine-tuned to catch sudden vibrations and deep pressure changes.

question: Why is a kidney infection (pyelonephritis) so dangerous for a pregnant woman?

options.A: It thickens the amniotic fluid until fetal movement stops completely
options.B: It stops the liver from producing essential blood-clotting proteins
options.C: It can trigger systemic sepsis and stimulate premature uterine contractions
options.D: It automatically causes permanent blindness in the developing fetus

explanation: High fever and severe infection put the whole body under massive stress, which can easily trick the womb into starting early labor.

question: An adult patient with severe liver disease starts bruising easily and bleeding from the gums. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: An acquired failure of the liver to produce clotting factors
options.B: An inherited defect in primary platelet aggregation
options.C: A congenital absence of von Willebrand factor
options.D: An inherited genetic mutation in the factor VIII gene

explanation: The liver is like the body's clotting factor factory! When it's sick, it can't make enough factors, leading to an acquired bleeding problem. You've got this!

question: As a nurse writing notes for a domestic violence survivor, how should you document physical injuries?

options.A: Avoid writing down statements made by the patient about the assault
options.B: Discard the documentation if the police are not immediately called
options.C: Include personal opinions about the partner's character in the notes
options.D: Use objective descriptions of the injuries and obtain patient consent

explanation: Correct! Always stick to clear, factual descriptions of what you see and get the patient's okay to protect their rights.

question: What must you always do right before an AED analyzes the heart rhythm or delivers a shock?

options.A: Check the patient's pupils with a penlight
options.B: Record the exact time on a chart
options.C: Ensure everyone is clear of the patient
options.D: Administer a dose of epinephrine

explanation: Always shout 'Clear!' and visually check that no one is touching the patient so the AED reads only their heart rhythm safely.

question: A patient is suffering from severe diarrhea and vomiting. What condition are they most at risk for?

options.A: Fluid volume deficit
options.B: Metabolic alkalosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Fluid volume excess

explanation: When fluids leave the body too fast from both ends, fluid volume drops quickly. That's why rehydration is usually the very first order of business!

question: Why is it important to check the medication label three times before instilling drops?

options.A: To follow hospital rules without any clear medical purpose
options.B: To catch any potential mistakes and ensure the right drug and dose are given
options.C: To make sure the expiration date is at least five years away
options.D: To help the patient memorize the name of their prescription

explanation: Triple-checking the label is a core safety habit that prevents giving the wrong medication or dose to a patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is the most important safety check before sending a patient for an MRI scan?

options.A: Checking for metal implants and devices inside the body
options.B: Confirming that the patient's blood sugar is normal
options.C: Making sure the patient has not eaten for two days
options.D: Checking if the patient is allergic to iodine dye

explanation: The MRI magnet is super strong! It can pull on metal objects or damage electronic devices like pacemakers.

question: Which healthcare professional helps recovering accident victims relearn everyday tasks like dressing, bathing, and eating?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Hospital pharmacist
options.C: Laboratory technician
options.D: Radiology specialist

explanation: Occupational therapists are fantastic at helping patients regain practical skills for daily living and independence.

question: Which group of men can be affected by male sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Only individuals with chronic kidney disease
options.B: Only men over the age of sixty-five
options.C: Exclusively adolescent males
options.D: Men across various age groups

explanation: Great job! Sexual health issues aren't just for older men—younger guys can face them too, often due to stress or other emotional factors.

question: What exactly do we mean by a "food myth" in healthcare?

options.A: A dietary belief that lacks scientific support
options.B: An official government nutrition guideline
options.C: A modern recipe created by clinical dietitians
options.D: A strict medical prescription for a disease

explanation: Food myths are unverified ideas about what food does to the body, passed along without scientific proof. Don't worry, once you spot them in clinical practice, they become much easier to address!

question: How do protective bed accessories help keep a patient's skin safe and healthy?

options.A: By acting as buffers between the body and the mattress
options.B: By increasing natural skin moisture and sweat production
options.C: By stimulating local sweat gland activity
options.D: By sealing skin pores to block bacteria entry

explanation: Spot on! These accessories create soft barriers that reduce direct friction and crushing pressure on vulnerable skin areas. You are doing great!

question: What is the safest way to bend your body when lifting a heavy patient or equipment?

options.A: By leaning to one side
options.B: At the waist only
options.C: At the hips and knees
options.D: With legs completely straight

explanation: Awesome! Always lift with your legs (knees and hips bent), not your back, to protect your spine from injury.

question: Which chemical gets released when tissues get injured, causing local blood vessels to widen?

options.A: Amylase
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Histamine is the chemical alarm bell! When cells are damaged, histamine rushes out, widening blood vessels and letting fluids flood the area—giving us the classic signs of inflammation.

question: A hospital ward plan fails the moment a sudden influx of accident victims arrives. What was missing from this plan?

options.A: Necessary flexibility and backup procedures
options.B: Too much focus on patient education
options.C: Input from doctors instead of experienced nurses
options.D: Goals that were far too ambitious and expensive

explanation: A plan that breaks during an emergency lacks the adaptability required in fast-paced healthcare settings.

question: A new mother has a tear involving her perineal muscles, but her anal sphincter is completely untouched. What kind of tear is this?

options.A: Third-degree tear
options.B: Second-degree tear
options.C: Fourth-degree tear
options.D: First-degree tear

explanation: When a tear goes deeper into the perineal muscles but stops before reaching the anal sphincter, we classify it as a second-degree tear.

question: Why is it tricky to use a stethoscope when a patient is lying on a very soft home bed?

options.A: Patients usually fall asleep immediately upon lying down on them.
options.B: Soft mattresses absorb all the sound waves from the stethoscope.
options.C: It makes proper patient positioning and organ assessment difficult.
options.D: Soft beds prevent the nurse from checking the patient's radial pulse.

explanation: Well done! A soft, unsupportive bed makes it hard to keep the correct posture needed to properly listen to the chest and tummy.

question: What is the main goal of taking medications for osteoarthritis?

options.A: To permanently cure the underlying bone disease
options.B: To stop all systemic autoimmune responses
options.C: To completely regenerate lost joint cartilage
options.D: To relieve pain and improve joint function

explanation: Well done! OA medications are meant to keep you comfortable and moving well, even though they don't cure the root condition.

question: What makes inhaled medications act so much faster than oral medications?

options.A: The massive surface area and rich blood supply of the lungs

options.C: The direct passage of drugs through the thick stomach wall
options.D: The strong muscular contractions found inside the bronchioles

question: How do common respiratory germs usually leave an infected person's body?

options.B: Via vector bites from blood-feeding insects like ticks

question: A village thinks their stream water is fine, but lab tests show it is full of harmful bacteria. The nurse steps in to treat the water. What kind of need is this?

options.A: Normative need
options.B: Expressed need
options.C: Comparative need
options.D: Felt need

question: Why do nurses keep a close eye on vaccine stock-outs?

options.A: To calculate the exact birth rate of the community

options.C: To ensure vaccines are always available for children
options.D: To reduce the number of required cold chain monitors

question: Which medication is typically prescribed as the first-line oral treatment for Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Regular insulin

options.C: Metformin
options.D: Glibenclamide

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of intraperitoneal administration?

options.B: Peritonitis

options.D: Inhalation pneumonia

question: Why do doctors prescribe strong iodine solutions like Lugol's solution right before a thyroid surgery?

options.A: To prevent allergic reactions to general anesthesia agents

question: Where does a non-competitive antagonist usually bind on a cell receptor?

options.A: Directly inside the active agonist binding groove

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of post-haemorrhage nursing care?

question: Even after physical withdrawal fades, why is quitting smoking still so tough?

options.B: Social laws make it illegal to stop smoking abruptly
options.C: The body continues producing natural nicotine forever
options.D: Psychological habits and environmental triggers remain deeply ingrained

explanation: The mental habit and social triggers stick around long after the physical chemicals leave the body. Don't worry if this takes time to master!

question: Why is a patient told not to eat or drink (NPO) before a laparoscopy?

options.A: To prevent the surgical instruments from getting dirty
options.B: To ensure the patient loses weight before surgery
options.C: To stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.D: To reduce the risk of aspiration during anesthesia

question: What classic sign might you notice in a patient with low blood calcium levels?

options.A: Dry skin and excessive hair growth
options.B: High blood pressure and rapid weight gain
options.C: Involuntary muscle spasms and cramps
options.D: Sluggish and severely delayed reflexes

explanation: Low calcium makes nerves super jumpy, causing muscles to twitch or cramp up. A classic clinical pearl for your nursing journey!

question: Which of these is an example of an intrinsic (internal) risk factor for a patient?

options.A: An improperly calibrated infusion pump
options.B: Muscle weakness from advanced age
options.C: A wet floor in the hallway
options.D: Poor lighting in the patient room

explanation: Intrinsic risks come from inside the patient's own body, like age-related muscle weakness, rather than from things around the ward.

question: A patient with untreated hypothyroidism will most likely show which sign?

options.A: Increased core body temperature
options.B: Decreased basal metabolic rate
options.C: Excessive weight loss despite high appetite
options.D: Rapid resting heart rate

explanation: Thyroid hormones are like your body's engine speed. Without enough of them, everything slows down—giving you a low metabolic rate, weight gain, and feeling cold all the time.

question: Why do symptoms of serum sickness usually take one to three weeks to show up after taking a new medication?

options.A: The liver must slowly break down the medicine into toxic metabolites.
options.B: The medication stays inactive in the stomach for several days before absorbing.
options.C: White blood cells are temporarily paralyzed by the foreign serum.
options.D: It takes time for the body to produce antibodies against the foreign proteins.

explanation: Think of it like a delayed response: your immune system needs a little time to recognize the foreign substance and build up antibodies.

question: A patient with food poisoning has bloody diarrhea. What does this usually mean?

options.A: Invasive mucosal damage in the intestinal wall
options.B: A mild reaction to harmless food preservatives
options.C: Normal healing of the stomach lining
options.D: Total absence of bacterial pathogens

explanation: Blood in the stool is a sign that the germ has actually invaded or broken through the delicate lining of the intestines, rather than just sitting in the gut making toxins.

question: A patient comes in with a warm, swollen, and painful knee after light activity. What is most likely going on?

options.A: Complete cessation of local osteoclast activity
options.B: Rapid mineralization of the surrounding bone matrix
options.C: Local inflammation and fluid accumulation in the joint
options.D: Immediate formation of a hard bony callus bridge

explanation: Warmth, swelling, and pain are classic signs of inflammation and fluid buildup inside the joint space. Great clinical deduction!

question: What is a poultice primarily made of?

options.A: A dry powder swallowed with plenty of water
options.B: A clear liquid injected directly into a vein
options.C: A soft, moist mass spread on a cloth
options.D: A hard plastic shell strapped onto a broken bone

explanation: A poultice consists of a moist, soft mixture applied externally using a piece of cloth or gauze. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h1)

question: How often should emergency crash carts and equipment usually be checked?

options.A: Once every month
options.B: Only after a code blue occurs
options.C: At the start of every shift
options.D: During annual hospital accreditation

question: A patient complains of mild tummy cramping and bloating shortly after a colonoscopy. What is the usual cause?

options.A: A severe allergic reaction to the sedative medication used
options.B: Internal bleeding starting in the lower intestinal wall
options.C: An infection caused by unsterilised examination tools

question: What is a major nursing priority right after a patient has heart valve surgery for endocarditis?

options.A: Stopping all antibiotic medications once the patient leaves the operating room

options.C: Restricting fluid intake completely to prevent any swelling

explanation: Great nursing care here means staying alert! We watch for any lingering infection and check the patient's brain function (neurological status) to catch any loose clots early.

question: What is a key sign that a post-abortion patient might be in severe pain?

options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin sclera
options.C: Increased heart rate and breathing rate
options.D: Sudden swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: When someone is in acute pain, their body's natural fight-or-flight response kicks in, causing their heart rate and breathing to speed up. Brilliant nursing observation!

question: Why are fast transport and clear communication so vital during a maternity emergency referral?

options.A: It allows the receiving hospital to prepare a private room
options.B: It prevents dangerous delays in treating life-threatening complications
options.C: It reduces the administrative paperwork for the nursing staff
options.D: It ensures the maternity home gets a refund for medical supplies

explanation: Spot on! Every minute counts in an emergency, and cutting down delays saves lives.

question: Which measure of central tendency is appropriate for nominal data like patient blood types?

options.A: Mode

options.D: Median

question: A patient is finding it hard to follow a strict diet and exercise plan. What should the team do?

options.A: Double the medication dose without telling the patient
options.B: Re-evaluate the plan with the patient to fit their actual lifestyle
options.C: Discharge the patient from community care for non-compliance
options.D: Report the patient to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Exactly! If a plan isn't working, we adjust it together with the patient so it fits their real life and is easy to follow.

question: Besides a poor diet, what is another very common cause of low iron levels in older adults?

options.A: Chronic gastrointestinal bleeding
options.B: Excessive absorption of iron in the stomach
options.C: Rapid destruction of iron by liver enzymes
options.D: High levels of stomach acid locking up iron

question: A patient says they want to save half their leftover antibiotics for a family member who might fall sick later. How should you respond?

options.A: Explain the dangers of sharing medications and encourage proper disposal
options.B: Write down instructions on which family member should take the leftover pills
options.C: Advise the patient to double the dose next time someone coughs
options.D: Praise the patient for being resourceful and saving money

explanation: Wonderful! As a nurse, you want to warmly educate patients on why sharing drugs spreads resistance and toxicity.

question: Which of the following is recognized as a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Standard immunization schedules
options.B: Routine antenatal blood screening
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding education
options.D: Female genital mutilation

question: What is the medical term when a baby is born without a fallopian tube?

options.B: Tubal agenesis
options.C: Uterine didelphys
options.D: Cervical stenosis

question: What does accountability mean for a nurse unit manager regarding finances?

options.B: Deciding how much profit the entire hospital should make
options.C: Setting the tax rates that fund the local health facility
options.D: Being responsible for staying within the assigned departmental budget

explanation: Accountability means managers must answer for how funds are spent in their unit and keep expenses within limits. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h2)

question: What type of pen ink is recommended for writing in manual health records to ensure longevity?

options.A: Washable water-based ink
options.B: Pencil for easy erasing
options.C: Red ink for all entries
options.D: Permanent black or blue ink

explanation: Permanent ink ensures that records do not fade, smudge with humidity, or get easily altered over time. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h7)

question: How are separate sanitary sewer networks different from combined systems?

options.A: They carry human wastewater in dedicated pipes separate from storm runoff
options.B: They only operate during daylight hours when industrial plants are open
options.C: They process all solid waste entirely on-site using chemical agents
options.D: They rely exclusively on open drainage ditches running alongside roads

explanation: Separate systems use one set of pipes for sewage and a completely different set for rainwater. This clever design keeps rain floods from overwhelming the treatment plant with raw waste!

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care for terminal patients at home?

options.A: Finding a surgical cure for advanced cancer
options.B: Testing new experimental drugs that reverse aging
options.C: Isolating the patient from all family and friends
options.D: Providing comfort, symptom control, and preserving dignity

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and managing symptoms to ensure the highest possible quality of life. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why do we need a team of different healthcare workers at the primary health care level?

options.A: Community members prefer being treated by multiple practitioners at once
options.B: Different health professionals are needed to cover diverse community needs
options.C: Hospital doctors refuse to travel outside urban administrative centers
options.D: Government policies require high staff counts to justify operational budgets

explanation: A community has all sorts of needs—from immunizations to health talks and treating minor illnesses. No single profession can do it all alone!

question: When would a manual blood pressure check with a stethoscope be a better choice than a digital machine?

options.B: When the patient has a very irregular heartbeat
options.C: When the hospital ward is completely quiet
options.D: When you are in a rush during a busy shift
